title: GPT-6 Astra constructs mutually orthogonal Latin squares that improve lower bounds at 33 orders
summary: GPT-6 Astra produced explicit mutually orthogonal Latin-square constructions that improve known lower bounds for N(n) at 33 values of n from 22 through 494. The standout construction gives four MOLS of order 22, completing the last open case needed to show N(n)≥4 for every n>10. The same paper reports resulting bounds at other orders and derives a strongly regular graph with parameters (484,126,40,30) from the order-22 construction; these connected consequences are counted once as one paper-level result.
ai_technology: OpenAI GPT-6 Astra, used through ChatGPT Pro and the OpenAI Codex harness
organization: Christopher D. Rosin (Constructive Codes; independent research project)

evidence.tested: GPT-6 Astra produced explicit mutually orthogonal Latin-square constructions that improve known lower bounds for N(n) at 33 values of n from 22 through 494.
evidence.unknown: This is an arXiv preprint. The constructions are finite combinatorial objects, checked by code written by the author and separately reconstructed/checked by Claude Opus 5.5 as reported in the paper. Counted once despite 33 parameter values and multiple corollaries.
evidence.ai_role: The author states GPT-6 Astra found all listed MOLS constructions and wrote their descriptions/code. The author wrote independent verification code for each construction; the paper also reports an independent Claude Opus 5.5 recreation and verification from the descriptions without the supplied code.
